To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the specific use and role of participatory approaches and patient involvement in data-intensive medical and health research is a crucial factor for the justification of this kind of research.
patient involvement in HBDR is often used as a rhetorical device and that this is problematic for the ethical evaluation of such research.
the use of participatory concepts within the field of data-intensive medical research is not justified and that it should be avoided in order to prevent ethical and practical problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to take patient participation and involvement in medical research seriously, and how this can contribute to the development of ethical and trustworthy data-intensive research.

the question of whether and under which conditions patient participation in HBDR and medical research is ethically justified, and if so, what the implications are for the design and governance of these research projects.
the critical ethical analysis of the specific use of participatory concepts and the role of patients in data-intensive medical and health-related research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ethical role and use of participatory approaches within data-intensive research should not be taken for granted, but needs to be justified in a more thorough way than is often the case.
participatory concepts should be used in HBDR and other medical research only when they meet these criteria.

, in the context of data-intensive research, the notion of participation should be taken seriously and that it is not only a question of the mere inclusion of patients in data-intensive medical and healthcare research but of the political and ethical dimensions of participation in the first place.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patient involvement in HBDR is not only a moral requirement, but also a practical necessity.
patient involvement should be taken seriously.
patient involvement is a necessary, but insufficient, condition for the justification of data-intensive research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ethical and practical challenges of participatory approaches are not to be underestimated and should be considered in research governance.
the notion of participation should not be used to legitimize data-intensive research, unless it is genuinely participatory.

the ethical relevance and practical implications of patient participation in data-intensive research in healthcare cannot be reduced to the question of informed consent and the protection of individual interests and autonomy.
